features.text: The patient is 38 years old and male.
The patient's back pain started after raking leaves yesterday.
The patient has pins and needles in his right foot.
The back pain is described as a tightening feeling and is constant.
The back pain does not radiate much, but the patient has pins and needles in his right foot.
The patient denies numbness or weakness in his lower extremities.
The patient denies changes in bowel or bladder function.
The patient has no history of back pain or neurological symptoms in the lower extremities.
The patient has no history of back surgery, trauma, diabetes, or spinal stenosis.
The patient mentions tingling in his right foot and that his partner noticed increased pain when standing.
The patient's back pain worsens when bending over and is relieved by sitting or hot showers.
The patient's partner noticed he was standing differently.
The patient's back pain is located in the lower back, near the middle of the spine.
The patient's back pain does not radiate to other parts of the body.
The patient had an X-ray done, which showed normal results.
The patient's partner noticed he was standing differently.
The patient has tingling in his right foot but no numbness or weakness in his legs.
The patient's tingling in the right foot feels like pins and needles.
The patient can still feel his foot and toes despite the tingling.
